newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong enters last month under British rule.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong enters last month under British rule.

text.p: The Royal Navy frigate HMS Chatham, command centre of Britain's military pullout from its last major colony, steamed towards Hong Kong on Sunday as the territory entered its last month under the Union Jack.
It was a Royal Navy landing party that planted the British flag claiming Hong Kong for Queen and country in 1841.
And it is from the decks of Royal Naval ships that the British will bid farewell to their last outpost in Asia.
At midnight on June 30, more than 156 years after Captain Edward Belcher scrambled ashore at Possession Point, Britain will honour its commitment to return Hong Kong to China.
HMS Chatham, a type 22 frigate, is due to arrive on Monday to serve as the floating command headquarters for the 61st and last Commander of British Forces, Major-General Bryan Dutton.

The Royal Yacht Britannia will convey the last Colonial Governor, Chris Patten, and Britain's Prince Charles, who will preside when Britain fulfils the terms of the 1984 Sino-British treaty governing the transfer of sovereignty.
The drawdown of the British garrison, the most visible expression of British sovereignty of Hong Kong, has cut the number of personnel from about 10,000 in the early 1990s to little more than 1,000.

On Saturday, Dutton presided over the disbandment of Britain's shortest-lived peacetime regiment. Just a month and a day before the wealthy community of 6.4 million people is returned to China, the job of the Hong Kong Logistic Support Regiment was done.
Nicknamed the 1,000-Day Regiment, although it served for a little longer, it was responsible for dismantling the garrison.
The Air Force Wessex helicopters were sold to Uruguay. The Navy's three Peacock class patrol boats to the Philippines.
Everything had to go. From boots to bedroom suites, cars to mess crockery, food, ammunition and sporting equipment.
Early last month, the troop ship RFA Sir Percivale sailed in to Hong Kong to pick up the garrison's remaining belongings.
The 1984 treaty on the handover binds China to maintaining Hong Kong's freewheeling lifestyle and a considerable degree self-government, but Beijing is responsible for defence.
A third group of 90 Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) troops drove across the border on Friday to join 106 colleagues already stationed in Hong Kong.
The soliders are preparing for the arrival of the full Chinese garrison, expected to number about 10,000 troops at its peak.
They inherit some of the world's most valuable real estate.
Agents estimate the swimming pool in the British military headquarters building in the Central business district occupies space worth HK$350 million ($45 million).

Many people in Hong Kong were horrified by the PLA's bloody crackdown of the student-led, pro-democracy movement around Beijing's Tiananmen Square in June 1989 and had regarded their arrival in the territory with trepidation.
Dutton, the first Commander of British Forces to visit China since the Communist Revolution of 1949, described the PLA advance guard as professionals.

"There is a desire for them to use Hong Kong as a window on the world to sell the PLA as a modern and effective force," he said The remaining British garrison troops of the Black Watch regiment, who will play a high profile role when Britain leaves in 30 days, will not sail away into the sunset. They will depart by air.
